newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate at 15-20 pct ahead of payment.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate at 15-20 pct ahead of payment.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate remained firm as banks kept funds for payment for a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bills issue on Thursday, dealers said.
The overnight was traded between 15 and 20 percent, against 13/20 percent on Monday.
"The overnight remains high because of the payment," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Bank Negara earlier announced that it accepted bids at an average yield of 6.955 percent, against 6.296 percent at the auction of 30-day bills amounting to 500 million ringgit on May 13.
Dealers said the payment for the bills would not affect the liquidity situation of the market as two Bank Negara bills issues worth a total one billion ringgit will mature on Thursday and Friday.
Earlier, interbank rates were also generally firmer as the market remained tight at the short end.
One- and two-week money were at 10.0/15.0 percent against 8.0/9.5 percent on Monday.
One-month money was at 9.0/9.5 percent and three- and six-month at 8.0/8.5 percent. They were all quoted at 7.5/8.0 percent on Monday.
One dealer said it was possible that the rates were kept high by the central bank partly as a move to fend off a fresh attack on the ringgit by speculators on Wednesday, a holiday in Malaysia.
At prevailing rates, it would be too expensive for players to maintain short ringgit positions, he said.

The rise in interbank rates started last Thursday after Bank Negara intervened aggressively in the foreign exchange market to stem the slide of the ringgit. The central bank was said to have sold around $1 billion worth of the dollar.
The intervention drained liquidity from the system, causing the market to be short and interbank rates to rise to unusually high levels.
